subsystems.name: Impactor spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: carries the mass that will deliver the momentum to the asteroid.

subsystems.name: Propulsion and launch
subsystems.role: puts the spacecraft on an intercept trajectory and fine-tunes it during cruise.

subsystems.name: Autonomous terminal guidance
subsystems.role: aims the spacecraft at the asteroid's centre of mass even though radio signals take minutes to arrive.

subsystems.name: Observer spacecraft
subsystems.role: flies alongside to measure the mass, shape and the actual change in orbit.

subsystems.name: Ground segment
subsystems.role: finds the asteroid, predicts the impact and commands the spacecraft.

buildSteps.title: Discover and track the asteroid
buildSteps.detail: Survey telescopes repeatedly photograph the sky; follow-up observations and radar refine the orbit over years until an impact probability can be computed.

buildSteps.title: Decide to deflect
buildSteps.detail: If the impact probability is high enough and there is time, a mission is designed to change the asteroid's velocity by a few centimetres per second — enough, years ahead, to miss Earth.

buildSteps.title: Design the encounter
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose the impactor mass and the closing velocity, typically several kilometres per second, so the delivered momentum exceeds the required nudge.

buildSteps.title: Build the impactor
buildSteps.detail: A compact spacecraft is assembled: structure, avionics, solar arrays, propulsion, and a camera plus computer for autonomous targeting.

buildSteps.title: Build the observer
buildSteps.detail: A second spacecraft is prepared to arrive before or shortly after impact, carrying cameras and radio-tracking equipment to measure the asteroid's mass and the resulting orbit change.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: Both spacecraft launch onto escape trajectories and coast for months or years, firing small thrusters to correct their paths.

buildSteps.title: Terminal approach
buildSteps.detail: In the final hours the impactor switches to autonomous navigation, recognising the asteroid against the star background and steering toward its centre.

buildSteps.title: Impact
buildSteps.detail: The spacecraft strikes at high speed; the collision throws out a plume of rock and dust, and the recoil from that ejecta adds extra push beyond the spacecraft's own momentum.

buildSteps.title: Measure the deflection
buildSteps.detail: The observer and ground telescopes track the asteroid's new orbit and estimate the momentum enhancement, confirming how much the orbit actually shifted.

prerequisites.why: the technique is useless unless a hazardous object is found and tracked years or decades in advance.
light-travel delay rules out joystick control, so the craft must identify and hit a small body on its own.
the nudge scales with closing speed, so reaching the asteroid fast matters more than spacecraft mass.
mass, shape and internal structure decide how the impact will behave and how big the deflection will be.
commanding and tracking the spacecraft across hundreds of millions of kilometres requires large ground antennas.

pathway.milestone: NASA's DART struck the moonlet Dimorphos in 2022 and measurably shortened its orbit, the first end-to-end test of the method
pathway.unlocks: proof that a kinetic impact can change a real asteroid's path.

pathway.milestone: ESA's Hera spacecraft reaches the same asteroid pair to survey the crater and measure Dimorphos's mass
pathway.unlocks: calibration of the momentum-enhancement factor, so future deflections can be sized correctly.

pathway.milestone: a reconnaissance-then-impact mission on an independent target, with the observer arriving before the strike
pathway.unlocks: deflection planning based on measured mass and shape rather than estimates.

pathway.milestone: a rapid-response capability: a stored or quickly assembled impactor that can launch within a few years of a credible threat
pathway.unlocks: deflection for objects discovered with only a short warning.

pathway.milestone: an integrated planetary defence architecture combining survey telescopes, repeated deflection and verification
pathway.unlocks: routine, tested protection against the larger near-Earth asteroids.
